guesses.breed: Domestic Shorthair (calico tabby / caliby with white)
guesses.reason: Short dense coat with brown mackerel tabby striping, patches of orange on the cheeks and paws, and a white muzzle, chest, and paws mark a classic tortoiseshell-tabby-with-white pattern common in random-bred cats.
The tabby striping on the legs and compact, sturdy-looking body resemble American Shorthair traits, though the large ears and slender face point away from purebred.
Notably large, tall, wide-set ears and a fine, wedge-leaning face hint at a slimmer Oriental-type influence.

breed.appearance: A young, slender shorthaired cat with a brown-gray mackerel tabby coat striped darkly across the forehead and legs, accented by soft apricot-orange patches on both cheeks around the eyes and on the toes. She has a crisp white blaze running down the nose to a white muzzle, a fluffy white bib covering the chest, and white front paws tinged with orange, plus a pink nose. Her ears are very large and upright with pale pink interiors, and her big round eyes are green-hazel, giving her a sweet, curious expression.
breed.fun_fact: Calico-tabby cats like Angela, often nicknamed 'calibies,' are almost always female and are known for their one-of-a-kind patchwork coats and spunky personalities!
